placements.quote: High-Acceptance DiElectron Spectrometer HADES at GSI, Darmstadt

summary.plain: A six-sector spectrometer around the beam line with a toroidal magnet, a ring-imaging Cherenkov detector for electrons and drift chambers for tracking, built to find rare electron-positron pairs among the particles from a collision.
summary.technical: HADES: ring imaging gas Cherenkov detector, tracking system of 6 superconducting coils with drift chambers, multiplicity and electron trigger array, two-stage trigger; 85% azimuthal coverage over 18-85 degrees, single-electron efficiency 50%, vector-meson mass resolution 2.5%.

technology.quote: HADES is a versatile magnetic spectrometer aimed at studying dielectron production in pion, proton and heavy-ion induced collisions.
technology.value: Versatile magnetic spectrometer with a ring imaging gas Cherenkov detector, six superconducting coils with a toroidal field, drift chambers and a multiplicity and electron trigger array
